text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A moratorium on Greek airforce flights over Cyprus takes centre stage in an internal Pasok dispute against Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
- Medical board chairman resigns over dispute on level of contributions to doctors' pension fund.
- The National Council is to debate the visit of British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind.
- Communist Akel sends a message of victory during municipal elections meeting in Paphos.
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos: Athens and Nicosia have worked out a common strategy to deal with Turkish threats in Cyprus.
- Britons are being recruited in the military bases to take over key positions.
- Luxury cars imported from England are sold at special offers in Cyprus.
- The U.S. is paving the way for a Turkish strike in Cyprus.
- Cypriot businessman says he will take archbishop to court if the Central Bank approves Vassiliko deal for 13 percent stock sale to Italcementi.
